frontier.hypothesis: The store sink is the SAME walk-back mechanism s12 exploited, one instruction further along, and it is closable by making find_cross_jump stop one insn EARLIER on the arm's 0x19 edge only - so that edge keeps its own 'sh $v0,0x286($s0)' and re-enters the shared block after the store, creating target's .L80028520 label and pinning path1's store in front of the argument set-up.
frontier.mechanism: Target's arm ends 'j .L80028520' with 'sh $v0,0x286($s0)' in the delay slot: the 0x19 edge merged only from 'addiu $a1,$zero,1' onward, keeping a duplicate store, while the 0xB edge merged all the way back to path1's 'li v0,0xB' at .L80028518. Our arm merges BOTH edges at the store, so the only live label sits BEFORE the 'sh' and sched2 is free to sink it into the jal's delay slot (the inverse of .claude/rules/defer-store-past-later-compute-into-jal-delay). Note that the five hand-placed do_calls/do_call2 entry points are already measured dead (H-s12-2), so the fix must come from the walk-back, not from label placement.
frontier.next_probe: Find a spelling in which the arm's 0x19 edge and path1 differ at the STORE insn while the 0xB edge still matches back to 'li v0,0xB'. Candidates to measure in one batch: (i) store the two constants through DIFFERENT C expressions on the two edges so the store's source operand differs pre-reload; (ii) give the arm's 0x19 edge an explicit s16 intermediate while the 0xB edge stores the variable directly; (iii) reverse which of path1's two edges is the fall-through so the merge anchors at the other end. Before spending probes, run 'pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_800283D0' on the banked 17-floor body and read the .jump2 dump: the arm's post-cross-jump block will show the exact merge anchor, which turns this from enumeration into one targeted edit. Score every form with 'bash tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s12/dif.sh'.

frontier.hypothesis: Cluster B (the nop-vs-'li v0,1' delay-slot fill at emitted slots 45/47 and again at 126) and the frontier-1 reorg residual s10 measured at insn 344 are ONE mark_target_live_regs / opposite_needed decision, not two.
frontier.mechanism: s10 proved cluster B does not move under any of the sixteen exit-form assignments. Ours fills the dispatch chain's last 'beq $v1,$v0' delay slot with 'li $v0,1' and leaves the following 'j' slot empty; target does the reverse. That is reorg stealing across the .L80028488 label in our build and declining to in target's - the same class of decision as the loss s10 measured at insn 344. This is now the only residual on the function with NO measured C-level dial at all.
frontier.next_probe: Locate the dispatch chain's final 'beq' insn UID in tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s10/iso_dumps/iso.dbr, grep that UID in tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s10/iso_dumps/dbr.log for its thr/simp lines, and check whether the steal is granted there for the same reason it is refused at 344. If both are opposite_needed decisions, clusters B and the frontier-1 nop collapse into one residual with one mechanism, and s10's open sub-question (why $v0 is in opposite_needed at insn 686 despite the REG_DEAD flush at label 347) becomes the single highest-value probe left on this function.
